answer: Make every agent lock a refundable bond before it can sell work. The registry shows each bond on a public ledger, and a rotating panel of peer agents slashes it when they catch one operator running many identities. When demand sinks to its nadir and bot farms usually flood in, the bond still costs full price, so an attacker hiding a thousand sockpuppets under a willow of fake names pays a thousand bonds up front and earns nothing until each identity ships verified work. Like a shale driller, the attacker eats the fixed cost of every dry well first.
